text: How will robots rise to power?
This is Elon Musk's Optimus. And you see, it wasn't built to rule. It was built to work.
So what's inside? Twenty-eight actuators. Six designs. Three rotary, three linear.
Rotary ones twist the joints. Linear ones push, like muscles.
And inside those? Planetary roller screws. One lifted a half-tonne piano.
The hands? Twenty-two degrees of freedom. Double the first version.
Power? A two point three kilowatt-hour pack, right in the torso.
Eyes? Autopilot cameras. Brain? Tesla's self-driving computer.
How does it learn? Humans show it. Suits, cameras, real tasks. Then it practises in simulation.
The plan? Tesla's factories first. Then other companies. Homes, later.
The goals? A line built for twenty thousand a week. And a price of twenty to thirty thousand dollars.
Of course, they won't rise to power. But it's beautiful to watch the rise of robots in our lifetime.
What should we take apart next?
